title: The duty that's yours
hookLine: Krishna comes down from eternity to earth: death is certain, this duty is yours, and people will talk
carry: svadharma: your own duty, win or lose
tomorrow: The right to act, never to the fruit
last: THE ATMAN: NEVER BORN, NEVER DIES.

cards: Good teachers do something you'll recognize. They give you the big, beautiful idea, see on your face that it hasn't landed, and try again from a plainer angle, closer to the ground.
Krishna has just told Arjuna about the eternal self, weapons that can't cut it, fire that can't burn it. Arjuna is still sitting there. So Krishna changes gear.
Suppose, he says in effect, you don't believe any of that. Here's why you still shouldn't grieve, and why you still have to stand up.

teach.h: DEATH IS CERTAIN FOR THE BORN.
teach.b: Argument one: even if you think the self is born and dies all the time, still don't grieve. In Sanskrit: jatasya hi dhruvo mrityur, dhruvam janma mritasya cha.

For the one who is born, death is certain; for the one who dies, birth is certain. You can't change what's inevitable. Beings are unseen before they're born, seen in the middle, and unseen again at the end.
What is there to lament? Argument two: dharma.

Look at your svadharma, Krishna says, the duty that's yours. Arjuna is a kshatriya, a warrior whose role is to protect, and this, Krishna says, is a righteous fight. Refuse it, and you abandon what's yours.
Argument three stings: people will talk. The great warriors will think you ran from fear. Your enemies will say things that shouldn't be said.
For someone honored, dishonor is worse than death. These three get more and more down to earth. Commentators notice it too; some say Krishna is meeting Arjuna where he is, before the deeper teaching.

teach.h: WIN OR LOSE, THE SAME. THEN ACT.
teach.b: Then the verse that turns toward it: sukha dukhe same kritva, labhalabhau jayajayau. Treat pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, and then act. Readers take this battlefield in different ways.
Some read it as a real war and a real duty. Gandhi read the whole Gita as a teaching about an inner fight, and drew nonviolence from it.

Either way, the core holds: there's work that's yours, and running from it doesn't make you free. That's svadharma, and it's why Hindus so often speak of faith as duty: to a family, a role, a stage of life.

how: Hindus often draw on Gita 2.31–2.38 when speaking of svadharma, the duty that belongs to one's own role and stage of life, and 2.38's call to treat gain and loss, victory and defeat alike is widely quoted.

o: the work that belongs to you
a law that's the same for all

games.q: Krishna's three arguments, and one turn — tap the pairs.
p: death is certain for the born

s: Krishna only argues from the eternal self
he also argues from plain facts: death is certain, this is your duty, people will talk.
Gandhi read the Gita's battle as an inner fight
and he drew nonviolence from it. others read it as a real war and a real duty.
2.38 says to act only when you're sure to win
it says to treat gain and loss, victory and defeat as the same, and then act.

games.q: you're Krishna. Arjuna is a warrior sworn to protect, and he wants to walk away from the one duty that's his. what do you point him to?
o: whatever wins him the most praise.
his svadharma: the work that's his, win or lose.
games.why: his svadharma. even if you doubt the eternal self, Krishna says, this duty is yours. treat victory and defeat the same, and act.

practice: Think of one role you actually hold, parent, friend, nurse, student, the one who keeps the family talking, and ask what piece of work in it only you can do, and you've been avoiding; don't judge it, just see it clearly.
Then try on Krishna's line, win or lose, the same, and picture doing that work without needing it to go well, just because it's yours.

wordCard.voice: Svadharma. One's own duty, the work that's yours. Death is certain for the born, there's work that's yours, and win or lose, you do it anyway.

orig.note: Sanskrit: sva, one's own, and dharma. the duty that belongs to you.

carryVoice: Your line: svadharma, your own duty, win or lose. Day one hundred sixty-three, done.
